issues.location: abstraction clause of parallel beta reduction
issues.finding: The second inductive clause uses N one-step beta-reduces N' instead of N parallel-beta-reduces N'. The later proofs explicitly use the parallel premise; leaving the source clause unchanged breaks their induction.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use N parallel-beta-reduces N' in the target rule and bounded comparison view; preserve frozen source bytes.

issues.finding: The proof's target abstraction substitutes R into N' although the lemma's right-hand side and induction hypothesis use the reduced replacement R'.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use substitution of R' into N' in the target display and bounded comparison view.

issues.location: redex case of substitution-compatibility lemma and its class-level prerequisites
issues.finding: The proof equates nested substitutions with a rearranged composition but gives no freshness conditions for binder x or composition lemma. Raw substitution composition can fail when x occurs free in the replacement: with N=y, Q=z, R=x, the two sides yield x and z. On alpha-classes one can choose a fresh binder, but this relies on the still-open alpha-safe substitution proof and an explicit composition argument.
issues.proposed_resolution: State the fresh-representative and composition dependency in target prose, retain the lemma statement, and keep proof certification pending until the class-level composition argument and OLP-0362 alpha proof are supplied.

translation_treatment: The target translates all prose and formal clauses, corrects the parallel premise and R-prime target, and flags the missing fresh-binder/composition justification. Structural QA is not proof certification. OLP-0362 and OLPL-273 remain open for the reader edition.
